newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on short covering, Egypt talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on short covering, Egypt talk.

text.p: Fund short covering amid signals the market was oversold and talk Egypt was seeking U.S. wheat boosted CBOT soft red winter wheat futures to a higher close, traders said.
"It was oversold but we're getting pretty far along on wheat harvest and we're running into demand too," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities, Des Moines, Iowa.
Another strong rally in nearby soybeans contributed to advances in the wheat pit as did rain in portions of the U.S. Midwest which was slowing harvest of the winter wheat crop.
Also traders said there was a rumor that Egypt was seeking 750,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for September/October shipment.

"We had some harvest interuptions and then the talk of Egypt coming in," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "They have not issued a tender yet but there is widespread belief that they will."
But U.S. grain exporters said they had received no indications Egypt would announce a tender for U.S. wheat.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 7-1/4 to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 9-1/4 at $3.25-3/4. September was up 9-1/2 at $3.34-1/4.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the July Monday fell to 16 percent and at Wednesday's close had recovered to 41.5 percent. A market with an RSI of 30 or less is considered oversold.
Funds bought roughly 20.0 million bushels of wheat, traders said. Rosenthal Collins bought six million bushels of September and Cargill Inc sold six million bushels of September, floor sources noted.
In spread trading, FIMAT Futures did one million bushels of September/December at 14 cents, premium December, sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 31,000 contracts, above the 22,348 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, Prudential Securities bought 400 September $4.40 calls at 1/8 cent and Farmers Commodities Corp sold 200 September, $3.20 puts at 5-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 8,000 contracts, above the 7,622 traded Tuesday.
